synth.volumeSharedChannel: Volume (%) — shared MIDI channel: the last value sent wins

synth.noteLengthSixteenth: Sixteenth note (a quarter of a beat)
synth.addZone: Draw a zone on the image
synth.programEditHint: Bank (A–P) and program (1–128) of this synth's MIDI channel: every change is sent to the instrument immediately (Bank Select then Program Change). “–” sends no Bank Select. Values are also learned from the MIDI input when the instrument transmits its changes, and saved in the session.

help.controls.load: Opens an image from your computer. Its pixels are interpreted as notes: each column of the reading grid is one step of the sequence, and each bright enough pixel is a note (pitch from brightness, force from saturation).
help.controls.reset: Resets every image adjustment (grid, contrast, brightness, vibrance, posterize, texture, clarity, simplify, auto levels) to their default values. The image is not reloaded from disk.
help.controls.rotate: Rotates the image in 90° steps. Reading direction and zones follow the displayed orientation.
help.controls.crop: Enables crop mode: draw a rectangle directly on the image to keep only that part.
help.controls.transform: Opens the image transform panel: fine rotation (-45° to +45°) and vertical/horizontal perspective. Apply to confirm, cancel to revert.
help.controls.transformGrid: Shows or hides the reading grid overlaid on the image.
help.controls.showOriginal: Shows the original, unadjusted image while held, to compare. Release to go back to the processed image.
help.controls.columns: Number of columns in the reading grid. Each column is played in turn; the finer the grid, the longer and more detailed the sequence. Changing this re-clips existing zones. Double-click the displayed count to type an exact value (refused if it exceeds the original image's width), or the slider to go back to the default value.
help.controls.contrast: Strengthens or softens the gap between dark and bright areas. High contrast makes the sequence more decisive: clear notes surrounded by silence. Double-click the slider to reset it to zero.
help.controls.brightness: Lightens or darkens the whole image. Too-dark pixels stay silent (below the synth's brightness threshold): this setting decides which ones play. Double-click the slider to reset it to zero.
help.controls.vibrance: Boosts or reduces color intensity, more subtly than raw saturation: muted colors are boosted more, while already-vivid colors stay natural. A pixel's saturation also sets the velocity (the force) of the note played. Double-click the slider to reset it to zero.
help.controls.posterize: Reduces the number of brightness levels (64 at most, 2 at least). With few levels the image becomes binary: each pixel is either silent or played at full force — great for rhythmic sequences. Double-click the slider to turn posterize off.
help.controls.texture: Boosts or softens fine detail in the image at a small scale. A high setting makes visual patterns and textures stand out in the sequence; a negative value smooths them out and reduces note-to-note "noise". Double-click the slider to reset it to zero.
help.controls.clarity: Strengthens or softens local contrast between areas, at a larger scale than texture. Emphasizes the image's patterns: sharper transitions between the sequence's sections. Double-click the slider to reset it to zero.
help.controls.simplify: Flattens near-uniform color areas while keeping edges crisp (bilateral smoothing). Combined with posterize, it produces clean, coherent zones — patterns that read more clearly musically. Double-click the slider to turn simplification off.
help.controls.autoLevels: Automatically stretches brightness onto the full available range (the outermost 0.5% of pixels are ignored). Flat or dark images then use the whole pitch and velocity spread. Colors are preserved: note pitch stays put. Click to toggle.
help.controls.help: Enables the contextual help mode: hover any control in the app to display a detailed explanation. Click again or press Escape to disable.
help.controls.mirror: Opens a mirror window of the image area on a second screen or projector, and puts it in fullscreen. Double-click the mirror to switch between fullscreen and a floating window you can drag to another screen. Click this button again to close the mirror. Active only when a second screen is connected.
help.controls.mirrorZones: Cycles through three zone displays in the projection window: every synthesizer's selected pixel zones, only those of the synths visible in the main window (eye button), or none at all. The main window always keeps its own per-synth visibility.
help.config.openFile: Opens the global configuration file: default settings for new synths, note ranges, enabled scales, maximum image size.
help.session.save: Saves the whole working session: the image and its adjustments, every synth with its zones and settings.
help.session.load: Reloads a previously saved working session.
help.synthList.add: Adds a new synthesizer. Each synth owns its zones on the image and plays in parallel with the others.
help.synthList.playAllStart: Starts every synth playing at once, or stops everything if at least one is already running.
help.synthList.panic: Immediately cuts all sounding MIDI notes. Useful if an external synthesizer is stuck on a note.
help.synth.midiPort: MIDI output port used by this synth: pick here the hardware or software instrument to drive. The "Wysiwyl (virtual — DAW)" port shows up as a MIDI input in your DAW (Ableton Live on macOS can't see virtual ports: use the IAC bus instead, see the README): select it as the MIDI source of an instrument track to drive a software instrument of the project.
help.metronome.syncBadge: The metronome follows the MIDI clock of a DAW or external device: the displayed tempo is the project's, and the tempo controls are disabled while the sync lasts. When the clock stops, the metronome keeps running at the last synced tempo and the controls are released.
help.metronome.clockMode: Source of the metronome's timing. Internal: the tempo set here is the only master. Auto sync: any incoming MIDI clock (a DAW's, an instrument's) takes over the tempo as long as it streams — this is the historical default behavior. Source…: only the MIDI clock received on the chosen input port is followed, other devices are ignored. Master: the app broadcasts its own MIDI clock (24 pulses per quarter note) to every MIDI output while a synth plays, with a Start on playback begin and a Stop on end, so external sequencers and arpeggiators follow this tempo.
help.metronome.clockSource: The MIDI input port whose MIDI clock the metronome follows in “Source…” mode. The “Wysiwyl (virtual — DAW)” entry is the app's own port, the one a DAW sends its sync to; the other entries are physical inputs, typically an instrument or interface clock.
help.metronome.masterBadge: The metronome broadcasts its own MIDI clock to every MIDI output: external devices and DAWs following it play at the tempo set here. The clock streams while at least one synth plays, with a Start message when playback begins and a Stop when it ends. The tempo controls stay active: they drive every follower live.
help.synth.renameHint: Double-click the synth's name to rename it.
help.synth.dragHandle: Drag to move this synth in the stack; the whole stack is renumbered accordingly.
help.synth.saveAsTemplate: Makes this synth the default template: every new synth will inherit its settings (mode, note range, note lengths, thresholds…).
help.synth.pickColor: Opens the palette to pick the synth's identification color, used for its zones and highlight on the image.
help.synth.remove: Removes the synth. For safety, a first click arms the button (red): click again within 3 seconds to confirm, otherwise the action is cancelled.
help.synth.toggleFullOptions: Switches to the compact view: only the playback controls (tempo, direction, loop, play…) remain visible. Click again to get every setting back.
help.synth.addZone: Adds a rectangular zone on the image: only the pixels inside it are read by this synth. A simple click selects or deselects a single pixel. Can be used while the synth is playing — the reading continues on the same pixel; an erasing drag touching the zone under the playhead is cancelled. Hold Alt (Option) to edit the manual silences instead: the rectangle silences the selected pixels it covers, or un-silences them when it overlaps existing silences.
help.synth.addZoneLasso: Free-hand selection: draw a closed shape on the image, every pixel it encloses (boundary included) toggles — an unselected pixel becomes selected, a selected pixel is removed. Releasing the mouse closes the shape with a straight line back to the starting point. Pixels of the zone being played are never removed. Usable during playback. Hold Alt (Option) to toggle the manual silences instead: an enclosed selected pixel becomes silent, a silent one plays again.
help.synth.selectAllZones: Adds the whole image as the reading zone.
help.synth.clearZones: Removes every reading zone of this synth, along with its manual silences. Emptying the zones while playing stops the synth and cuts the sounding note.
help.synth.toggleHighlight: Shows or hides this synth's zone highlight on the image.
help.synth.toggleSort: When active, the selected pixels are read following their absolute position in the image, in the chosen reading direction — one continuous merged sweep. Otherwise each zone is read in full, one after the other, in the order they were drawn. The playhead stays on its pixel when toggling.
help.synth.tempoRatio: Per-synth tempo ratio, relative to the global metronome tempo. 1/2 = twice as slow.
help.synth.readingDirection.leftToRight: Sequence reading direction: left to right.
help.synth.readingDirection.rightToLeft: Sequence reading direction: right to left.
help.synth.readingDirection.topToBottom: Sequence reading direction: top to bottom.
help.synth.readingDirection.bottomToTop: Sequence reading direction: bottom to top.
help.synth.toggleLoop: Enables looping: the sequence plays over and over. When off, playback stops at the end of the sequence.
help.synth.toggleBackAndForth: Back-and-forth playback: the sequence plays forward then bounces backward between both ends.
help.synth.rewind: Puts the playhead back at the start of the sequence.
help.synth.stepForward: Advances playback by a single step (one grid column), without starting continuous playback.
help.synth.volume: Channel volume of this synth, as a percentage (0–100). Sent as MIDI CC 7 to the instrument, and reasserted when playback starts. Scroll over the field to adjust the value. Caution: CC 7 addresses the MIDI channel, not the synth — synths sharing the same port and channel override each other, the last value sent winning.
help.synth.noteLengthSixteenth: Note length for pixels of this brightness: sixteenth note, very short — a click.
help.synth.noteLengthEighth: Note length for pixels of this brightness: eighth note, short.
help.synth.noteLengthQuarter: Note length for pixels of this brightness: quarter note, the default duration.
help.synth.noteLengthHalf: Note length for pixels of this brightness: half note, sustained — notes slightly overlap.
help.synth.noteLengthWhole: Note length for pixels of this brightness: whole note, strongly sustained.
help.synth.reverseNoteLength: Reverses the brightness → duration mapping: dark pixels give long notes, bright ones short notes.
help.synth.noteSustain: Toggles the note articulation. Active (sustained): each note holds for its full duration, the Note Off only arriving with the next note. Inactive (pizzicato): the Note Off is sent immediately after the Note On — the instrument releases the note and its natural decay (the sound's release phase) shapes the tail, like a plucked string. The reading rhythm is unchanged: note lengths still pace the pixels.
help.synth.toggleRed: Enables or disables the red channel of the image: only pixels with this color component (above the threshold) are played.
help.synth.toggleGreen: Enables or disables the green channel of the image: only pixels with this color component (above the threshold) are played.
help.synth.toggleBlue: Enables or disables the blue channel of the image: only pixels with this color component (above the threshold) are played.
help.synth.noteRangeTitle: The pitch range every note of this synth is played in. The raw note derived from the pixel is rescaled proportionally: the pitch rises gradually across the whole selected range as the hue (or the channel value) increases.
help.synth.noteRangeBass: Restricts notes to the bass range. The pitch rises gradually from the low to the high bound of the range as the hue (or the channel value) increases.
help.synth.noteRangeMedium: Restricts notes to the medium range. The pitch rises gradually from the low to the high bound of the range as the hue (or the channel value) increases.
help.synth.noteRangeTreble: Restricts notes to the treble range. The pitch rises gradually from the low to the high bound of the range as the hue (or the channel value) increases.
help.synth.scale: Scale this synth's notes are quantized to: every note derived from a pixel is snapped to the nearest degree of the chosen scale, staying within the enabled tessitura — both constraints are respected. Chromatic = no quantification, every semitone allowed. The scale is shared by the monophonic note and the three polyphonic voices.
help.synth.scaleRoot: Tonic (starting note) of the chosen scale. E.g. natural minor + A = A minor: degrees are counted from this note.
help.synth.hueShift: Shifts the hue of pixels before the note conversion: each degree rotates the color circle, so the same image yields different notes. Handy to explore variations of the same reading zone.
help.synth.brightnessThreshold: Brightness window within which a pixel is audible: below the low bound or above the high bound, the pixel stays silent. Muted pixels in this synth's zones are veiled in black, with the 𝆝 symbol in its color when cells are large enough. The two sliders adjust the bounds.
help.synth.velocityRange: Note velocity (force) window. The actual force of each note depends on the pixel's saturation, rescaled between the low and the high bound. The two sliders adjust the bounds.
help.synth.velocityRelative: Toggles the velocity mode. Active (relative): the pixel's saturation is rescaled onto the whole min–max range, so the entire range is always used. Inactive (clamp): the velocity is computed on the native 1–127 range, then brought to the nearest bound when outside the window — weak saturations floor at min, strong ones ceiling at max, with no compression in between.
help.synth.programEditHint: Bank and program of this synth's MIDI channel. Selecting a bank (A–P = Bank Select MSB 0–15) and a program (1–128) sends them immediately: the instrument is reconfigured even if it transmits nothing itself. Values are also learned from the MIDI input, saved in the session, and resent to the instruments when it loads.
